issue_context.title: Kubectl .lock file is ambiguous
issue_context.body:
<!-- Please use this template while reporting a bug and provide as much info as possible. Not doing so may result in your bug not being addressed in a timely manner. Thanks!

If the matter is security related, please disclose it privately via https://kubernetes.io/security/
-->


#### What happened:

``` bash
KUBECONFIG=/dir1/config kubectl config use-context ctx --kubeconfig=/dir2/config
```
Use `/dir1/config.lock` and `/dir2/config`

#### What you expected to happen:

Use `/dir2/config.lock` and `/dir2/config`

#### How to reproduce it (as minimally and precisely as possible):

#### Anything else we need to know?:

- Kubernetes version (use `kubectl version`):

- OS (e.g: `cat /etc/os-release`):
- Kernel (e.g. `uname -a`):
- Install tools:
- Network plugin and version (if this is a network-related bug):
- Others:
comments: kubectl locks all files being read or written. I'm pretty sure but not positive that even if you pass `--kubeconfig` other files may be read.

I found it has been fixed in 1.20, https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/93293
Close this
do we need to backport this? what version were you on?

1.19, Of course it would be better if it could be backport. although i think upgrading Kubectl is not a problem.

Due to the patch of #93293, I think it is necessary to clean up some of the code here that will no longer be used https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/100455#discussion_r599216408

review_comments:
Is this check really sufficient to ensure that none of the other files will be read / written to below?
I don't think it is.

Why should possible sources contain files we won't actually read|write if that is the case? This seems brittle.

Only `writeCurrentContext` and `writePreferences` use `GetLoadingPrecedence `, and `IsExplicitFile` is also used first

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/1822523afb68f33df242b1c43590154f1a361784/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/clientcmd/config.go#L196-L206
